evidence.quote: Our experiments also cover a fixed set of agent models and benchmark tasks, so broader generalization to other environments and user populations remains to be studied.
our evaluation of rule updates is primarily based on controlled component diagnostics rather than extended interactions in which user preferences repeatedly change.

Although we separately validate the simulation procedure against real user correction histories, simulated feedback cannot fully capture the diversity and unpredictability of long-term human–agent collaboration.

TellOnce relies on correctly interpreting what a user wants the agent to learn and when that requirement should apply. Ambiguous or context-dependent corrections may be difficult to interpret reliably.

Moreover, not every learned requirement can be checked automatically from available execution evidence. In such cases, TellOnce retains the requirement as behavioral guidance, while semantic checking may also introduce judgment errors.
Rule learning, selection, and checking also introduce additional computation, which is not explicitly matched across methods in our end-to-end comparisons.
